program_name:
Volcanology. STANDALONE PROGRAMME, NOT A CURRICULUM — it has its own course code, its own SUA-CdS record, its own Didactic Regulations and its own Didactic Coordination Commission (CCD).

OFFICIAL DENOMINATIONS. The English denomination and the registered course name are identical: the Federico II course register (corsi.unina.it API record for the course) gives "nomeCds": "VOLCANOLOGY" and "nomeCdsEng": "VOLCANOLOGY". The Italian legal denomination recorded in the SUA-CdS is "Vulcanologia" — the Didactic Regulations, Art. 1, quote the SUA-CdS framework "General CdS Information" as: "CdS name in Italian - Vulcanologia / CdS name in English - Volcanology / Class LM-74 Geological Sciences and Technologies / Teaching language - English". The programme markets itself as "Master of Science in Volcanology" on its dedicated website (volcanology.unina.it) and as "Laurea Magistrale in Volcanology" on unina.it. All refer to the same degree.

UNIVERSITY COURSE CODES — TWO CODES EXIST AND THIS MATTERS FOR APPLICANTS. There are two records because the programme was re-established under Italy's 2023-24 degree-class reform:
  - DH1 = the CURRENT, ACTIVE course, degree class LM-74 R (reformed class). API flags: "attivo": true, "esaurimento": false, "lastSuaYear": 2026, "claMiurCod": "LM-74 R". This is the code a 2026/27 applicant enrols into. URL: https://www.corsi.unina.it/DH1
  - P67 = the OLD course, degree class LM-74 (pre-reform), activated a.y. 2022/23. API flags: "attivo": false, "esaurimento": true (i.e. "in esaurimento" — closed to new enrolments, running only until currently-enrolled students graduate), "lastSuaYear": 2024. The corsi.unina.it P67 page itself is headed "Regulations valid for students enrolled up to the 2024/2025 a.y.". URL: https://www.corsi.unina.it/P67
Most public-facing pages (orientamento.unina.it, volcanology.unina.it) have not yet been updated and still show the P67-era data.

STRUCTURE. Two years, four terms, 120 CFU/ECTS, no curricula/tracks (a single undivided study path). Delivered by the Department of Earth, Environment and Resources Sciences (DiSTAR — Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra, dell'Ambiente e delle Risorse), School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences (Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base). Established under a formal agreement (Convenzione Quadro di Collaborazione Scientifica e Didattica) between Federico II and INGV — Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, with the Osservatorio Vesuviano (founded 1841, the oldest volcano observatory in the world) as the operational partner; INGV-OV researchers co-teach and host the compulsory internship. unina.it describes it as "the first course in Italy that has as its central theme volcanology in its entirety".

Coordinator (course register, current): Daniele Morgavi, daniele.morgavi@unina.it. Degree Programme Director / orientation contact on the orientamento course sheet and in the SUA-CdS: Prof. Paola Petrosino, paola.petrosino@unina.it, tel. 081 2538327. Contact for international students: Diana Barra, diana.barra@unina.it, tel. 081 2538133. Programme office: master.volcanology@unina.it (Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00).
level:
Master (second-cycle) — Italian "Laurea Magistrale", 2-year Master's degree, 120 CFU (University Educational Credits / ECTS), 4 terms. Course register: "tipoCorsoDes": "Laurea Magistrale", "durataAnni": 2. Didactic Regulations, Art. 9: "The legal duration of the Degree Program is 2 years" and "The student must acquire 120 CFU", awarded "by passing examinations, not exceeding 12, and the performance of other training activities". Each CFU = 25 hours of total student workload; contact hours per CFU are 8 (lectures), 12 (guided/laboratory exercises) and 16 (field activity) — an unusually field-heavy profile.

Entry qualification required: a first-cycle degree. The orientamento course sheet header states "Degree required Laurea I Livello". SUA-CdS 2026 (framework REQ_ACC): "Il titolo di studio richiesto è la laurea, triennale o quinquennale" (the required qualification is a degree, three-year or five-year).

Programme structure (P67-era study plan published on the orientamento course sheet; the DH1/LM-74 R plan is an updated version of the same design): Year 1 compulsory — Physical Volcanology 9 CFU, Magmatology 6, Geochemistry of volcanic fluids 9, Volcano seismology and geodesy 6, Geophysical exploration of volcanic systems 6, Statistics and mathematics for geosciences 6, Volcanotectonics 6; plus 12 CFU chosen from Slope stability in volcanic areas / Volcanic landforms and landscapes / GIS and remote sensing in volcanic areas / Experimental petrology / Geoarchaeology in volcanic areas (6 CFU each). Year 2 compulsory — Frontiers in multiparametric volcano monitoring 6, Physical modelling of volcano processes and dynamics 6, Volcano hazard and risk assessment 6; plus 6 CFU chosen from Hydrogeology of volcanic areas / Advanced isotope geochemistry / Field volcanology; Thesis 24 CFU; Internship 6 CFU; Italian (for foreign students) / other activities 6 CFU.

The thesis (24 CFU) must contain original experimental data. Didactic Regulations, Art. 2: the thesis "must rigorously include an experimental data acquisition part". Final exam format (programme Documentation page): a 15-minute presentation of original research plus three committee questions; up to 9 bonus points added to the weighted average (0-2 graduating on time, 0-2 referee evaluation, 0-5 committee); honours (cum laude) requires a virtual grade of at least 112/110 and unanimous committee approval.

Attendance: Didactic Regulations, Art. 10 — lecture attendance is "strongly recommended but not compulsory", except where an individual course sheet requires it; attendance at credit-bearing seminar activities is compulsory. Delivery is "conventional" (in person) by design, so that students can use the Neapolitan volcanic area as an open-air laboratory.
teaching_language:
English — 100% English-medium, with no Italian-taught component and no Italian-language entry requirement. This is confirmed by five independent official sources with no conflicting evidence:
  (a) orientamento.unina.it course sheet header: "Language ENG".
  (b) Course register API record for DH1 (and P67): "linguaIta": "INGLESE", "linguaEng": "English".
  (c) Didactic Regulations, Art. 1, quoting the SUA-CdS: "Teaching language - English".
  (d) Didactic Regulations, Art. 4: "Considering that the course is delivered entirely in English, proficiency in the English language equivalent to European level B2 or higher, duly certified, is required."
  (e) SUA-CdS 2026 course description: "Il percorso di studi è rivolto a una platea studentesca internazionale e, pertanto, tutte le attività sono previste in inglese, per cui il corso di LM si configura come corso 'a carattere internazionale'" (the programme is aimed at an international student body and therefore all activities are delivered in English, so the LM is configured as a course "of international character").

CONSEQUENCE FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS — NO ITALIAN B2 REQUIRED. Because the programme is English-taught, the University's blanket Italian B2 rule for Italian-taught degrees does not apply. international.unina.it/admission-regulation: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." The same page adds that an international English certificate (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge) is nevertheless "useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation".

Italian is offered as an optional support subject, not as a barrier: the study plan carries "Italian (for foreign students)/other activities 6 CFU", and students who do not need Italian language courses may, on request to the LM committee, convert those 6 CFU into additional traineeship activity (orientamento course sheet, Traineeship opportunities).

The teaching department is DiSTAR, whose official published address (department website footer) is: "Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo (Ed. 10), Via Vicinale Cupa Cintia 21, 80126 NAPOLI", tel. +39 081 2532146, dip.scienze-terambris@unina.it.

The orientamento course sheet, "Links Department", confirms both the campus and the fact that student-facing services sit in the same building: "The courses are held at DiSTAR (Dipartimento d Scienze della Terra, dell'Ambiente e delle Risorse), Monte Sant'Angelo Campus Builing 10, Via Vicinale Cupa Cintia 21 - 80126 Naples, where also the library and the student bureau are located."

MINOR BUILDING-LABEL DISCREPANCY (does not affect the campus). Both refer to the same DiSTAR premises on the Monte Sant'Angelo complex; "Ed. 10" is the label used in the department's own official postal address and on the orientamento sheet, so "Building 10" should be treated as authoritative and "building L" as a legacy label. GETTING THERE (orientamento course sheet, Connections): "You can reach the campus by bus from the Campi Flegrei metro station (Linea 2 Trenitalia), from Mostra station of Cumana railway and by several private buses from other towns in the neighborhoods of Naples."

SECOND SITE — INGV-OSSERVATORIO VESUVIANO. Internships are hosted off-campus at INGV-OV: "INGV-OV will host students for internships in the headquarters of Via Diocleziano, 3 km far from the campus site." Field teaching takes place across the Neapolitan volcanic district (Campi Flegrei, Vesuvius, Ischia), and students may also be placed at INGV operations centres on Vulcano and Stromboli, at other INGV offices, at foreign volcano observatories, or at the Italian Civil Protection offices in Rome.

Graduation-administration site: the Student Administration Office of the Faculty of Science is in the "Centri Comuni" building at the same Monte Sant'Angelo campus (programme Documentation page).
degree_class:
LM-74 — Italian degree class LM-74, "Scienze e tecnologie geologiche" (Geological Sciences and Technologies). The brief's value is CORRECT but INCOMPLETE for a 2026/27 applicant, and the precise code has changed:
  - CURRENT course DH1: "claMiurCod": "LM-74 R", "claMiurDes": "Scienze e tecnologie geologiche". The suffix "R" marks the REFORMED degree class introduced by Italy's 2023-24 revision of the classi di laurea. This is the class a student enrolling in 2026/27 graduates in.
  - LEGACY course P67: "claMiurCod": "LM-74", "claMiurDes": "Classe delle lauree magistrali in Scienze e tecnologie geologiche" — the pre-reform class, now closed to new enrolments ("esaurimento": true).

The class is also confirmed in the Didactic Regulations title block ("DIDACTIC REGULATIONS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAM VOLCANOLOGY / LM-74"), in Art. 1 ("the CdS in Volcanology (class LM-74)"), in the orientamento course sheet header ("Degree class LM-74"), and in the current regulation's own file name, "Regolamento LM74 R Volcanology.pdf".

WHY THE CLASS MATTERS PRACTICALLY. LM-74 is the class that gives access to the Italian State Examination (esame di Stato) for registration as a professional geologist. orientamento course sheet: "After graduation you can take the Italian national exam to become a professional geologist." SUA-CdS: "il laureato LM-74 può accedere all'esame di stato per l'esercizio della professione del Geologo" (the LM-74 graduate may sit the State exam to practise as a Geologist). Didactic Regulations, Art. 3, lists among employment fields "Freelance geologists, subject to passing a state examination for registration with the geologists' register".

OTHER OFFICIAL IDENTIFIERS: School code 040463 (Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base); Department code 040146 (DiSTAR); teaching site "NAPOLI"; activation year 2021 (DH1 record) / 2022 (P67 record, first intake a.y. 2022/23).
admission_type:
OPEN ACCESS WITH A COMPULSORY ELIGIBILITY INTERVIEW — the two halves of this description must be read together, because taking either one alone gives a misleading picture.

1) NO NUMERUS CLAUSUS, NO RANKING, NO BANDO. The orientamento course sheet header states "Admission Libero" (free/open access). There is therefore no competitive selection, no merit ranking, no admission call (bando) and no capped number of places. Applicants are not competing against each other. The University confirms the administrative consequence: for open-access courses "La procedura di immatricolazione ai corsi ad accesso libero è solo telematica ed è effettuata attraverso la piattaforma Segrepass" (unina.it, "Immatricolarsi alla Federico II per l'a.a. 2026/2027").

2) BUT ADMISSION IS NOT AUTOMATIC — A PERSONAL-PREPARATION INTERVIEW IS MANDATORY. Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it" and "The verification of the student's personal preparation is carried out through an interview." A three-professor committee, appointed annually by the programme's Teaching Commission, assesses the candidate's background and issues a written clearance ("nulla-osta") without which the student cannot enrol. The interview is a PASS/FAIL eligibility gate, not a scored competition: nothing the candidate does produces a rank.

3) EXEMPTION FROM THE INTERVIEW. Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "Bachelor's degree graduates who have obtained a bachelor's degree in the L34 class (Geological Sciences) or in the class 16 ex D.M. 509/1999, with a score higher than 90/110, are exempt from the verification and obtaining clearance." In practice this exempts a subset of Italian geology graduates only; essentially every international applicant goes through the interview.

4) TWO SEPARATE ADMINISTRATIVE ROUTES, DEPENDING ON CITIZENSHIP AND RESIDENCE.
  - Italian / EU citizens, and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or an EU country (no visa needed): direct route. Send academic documents to the Course Coordinator for the eligibility assessment, then enrol online via Segrepass. Signposted on both the orientamento sheet and volcanology.unina.it/about: "For Italian students, please see https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do". international.unina.it (EU Students): such candidates "have unrestricted access to university courses if you hold a foreign qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification", and must "send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in".
  - Non-EU citizens resident abroad (visa needed): compulsory pre-enrolment on the MUR Universitaly portal, validated by the University, followed by a study-visa application. The Coordinator's eligibility assessment produces a PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER, which is the document the embassy needs. Programme news item (6 May 2026): "The Coordinator of the programme will be provided with the applicants' curricula in order to assess their eligibility. Where the requirements are met, a pre-acceptance letter will be issued. Please note that the pre-acceptance letter is a mandatory document for obtaining a study visa".

5) NO ENTRANCE TEST OF ANY KIND. Not TOLC, not SAT, not a national MUR test. The national admission tests referenced on international.unina.it apply only to Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine and Architecture — not to this programme.

6) PRE-ENROLMENT IS NOT ADMISSION. Official 2026/2027 non-EU brochure (DiSTAR/Federico II): "Pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. Applicants must meet all academic and admission requirements." And: "The issuance of a visa does not automatically guarantee enrolment at the University."
academic_requirements:
There are three cumulative conditions: a first-cycle degree, a credit (CFU) profile in specified scientific sectors, and a verified personal preparation. All three come from the current SUA-CdS 2026 (a.y. 2026/27) and the Didactic Regulations.

A) ENTRY QUALIFICATION
SUA-CdS 2026, framework REQ_ACC: "Il titolo di studio richiesto è la laurea, triennale o quinquennale. Nel caso di titoli di studio universitari conseguiti all'estero, l'idoneità di tali titoli di studio sarà valutata dal Comitato di Coordinamento, tenendo conto della legislazione e degli accordi internazionali vigenti." (The required qualification is a degree, three-year or five-year. For university qualifications obtained abroad, their suitability is assessed by the Coordination Committee, taking account of legislation and international agreements in force.)
Didactic Regulations, Art. 4, states it as: "applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma, or another foreign qualification deemed suitable by the Course Council, or possess a three-year degree in the L-34 class."
A foreign bachelor's degree of at least three years is therefore acceptable; there is no requirement that it be Italian.

B) CREDIT (CFU) REQUIREMENT — 60 CFU MINIMUM, WITH A 24 CFU GEOSCIENCE CORE
This is the requirement that most often disqualifies non-geology applicants, and it TIGHTENED in the current SUA-CdS. The 2026 wording uses Italy's new GSD (gruppi scientifico-disciplinari) codes:
SUA-CdS 2026, REQ_ACC: "lo studente deve aver conseguito almeno 60 CFU nei gruppi scientifico disciplinari (GSD) CHEM, PHYS, MATH, GEOS e 08/CEAR-05, di cui obbligatoriamente almeno 24 CFU nei settori scientifico disciplinari facenti capo ai GSD 04/GEOS-01, 04/GEOS-02, 04/GEOS-03, 04/GEOS-04 e nei settori scientifico disciplinari CEAR-05/A Geotecnica e PHYS-05/B Fisica del sistema Terra, dei pianeti, dello spazio e del clima."
In plain terms: at least 60 ECTS across chemistry, physics, mathematics, geosciences and geotechnical engineering, OF WHICH AT LEAST 24 ECTS must be specifically in geoscience sectors (GEOS-01 to GEOS-04), geotechnics (CEAR-05/A) or Earth/planetary/space/climate physics (PHYS-05/B).
The earlier (P67-era) formulation of the same rule, still shown in the older Didactic Regulations text and useful for mapping old Italian SSD codes, was: "graduates must have acquired at least 60 CFU (University Credits) from the following Scientific Disciplinary Sectors: GEO/01-GEO/12, FIS/01-FIS/08, MAT/01-MAT/09, CHIM/01-CHIM/04, CHIM/09, CHIM/12, ING-INF/05, INF/01."
The programme's own website states the 24-credit core explicitly and in English: volcanology.unina.it/about — "Alternatively, a minimum of 60 CFU (ECTS) in geologic, mathematics, chemistry and informatics related subjects, of which at least 24 CFU (ECTS) in geological, geophysics and geotechnical subjects".

NOTE A PUBLISHED INCONSISTENCY ON THE ENTRY DISCIPLINE. The orientamento course sheet gives a broader and more permissive summary — "Bachelor's (3 years minimum) in Geology, Physics or Chemistry or equivalent degree" — whereas volcanology.unina.it/about says "A Bachelor (min 3 years) in Geology or equivalent degree". The binding text is the SUA-CdS/Regulations credit rule above, which a physics or chemistry graduate can satisfy only if they also hold the 24 CFU geoscience/geotechnics/Earth-physics core. Both pages agree that non-standard profiles are considered individually: "Alternative careers or academic backgrounds will be evaluated on a case by case basis" (orientamento) / "by the admission committee" (volcanology.unina.it).

C) PERSONAL PREPARATION — ASSESSED, NOT ASSUMED
SUA-CdS 2026, REQ_ACC: "per l'accesso al corso di Laurea Magistrale in Volcanology, è richiesta una formazione di base nelle discipline matematiche, fisiche e chimiche e un'adeguata conoscenza geologica di base." (a basic grounding in mathematics, physics and chemistry and adequate basic geological knowledge is required). The mechanism is the interview described under entry_exam_or_test.

D) ENGLISH B2 — see language_requirements. Art. 4 treats it as an admission requirement, not a formality.

E) WHAT THE COMMITTEE'S CLEARANCE ALSO DOES. The nulla-osta is not merely a yes/no. SUA-CdS 2026, REQ_ACC_2: "Il nulla-osta contiene le indicazioni della Commissione sul piano di studi, volte a integrare il percorso formativo pregresso dello studente e a evitare possibili ripetizioni." (The clearance contains the Committee's indications on the study plan, aimed at integrating the student's prior education and avoiding possible repetitions.) So an admitted student may receive a tailored study plan.

F) NO OFA / NO REMEDIAL DEBT ROUTE. Unlike bachelor's admission, there is no "additional training obligation" mechanism here: a candidate who lacks the 60/24 CFU must acquire them before enrolling. The University's general rule for open-access master's degrees (orientamento FAQ, "Corsi di laurea magistrale biennale ad accesso libero") is explicit: "Posso immatricolarmi se non possiedo i requisiti di accesso? No. Prima di immatricolarsi è necessario acquisire i requisiti di accesso richiesti" — and if a student enrols without them, "la Segreteria Studenti avvierà il procedimento di annullamento dell'immatricolazione" (the enrolment will be annulled). Missing credits can be acquired by enrolling in single courses (Corsi Singoli).
entry_exam_or_test:
NO written entrance examination, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO national MUR test, NO portfolio — but there IS a COMPULSORY ADMISSION INTERVIEW (colloquio) that functions as a pass/fail eligibility gate. This is the single most commonly misunderstood point about this programme: "Admission Libero" on the orientamento sheet means no numerus clausus, not "no assessment".

WHAT THE INTERVIEW IS
Didactic Regulations, Art. 5 (identical in substance to SUA-CdS 2026, framework REQ_ACC_2):
  - "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it." (So the 60/24 CFU check comes FIRST; the interview is the second gate.)
  - "The verification of the student's personal preparation is carried out through an interview. A special committee, established within the Teaching Commission of the Course of Study, evaluates the congruence and suitability of the student's basic preparation intending to enroll."
  - "The Verification Committee consists of three professors, representing the various disciplinary fields of Earth Sciences, and is appointed annually by the Teaching Commission of the Course of Study."
  - "Based on the student's curriculum vitae and the outcomes of the interview, the Committee issues a clearance for enrollment in the Master's degree program. The clearance includes the Committee's recommendations regarding the study plan, aimed at integrating the student's previous educational path and avoiding possible redundancies."

OUTCOME: a "nulla-osta" (clearance) — a binary eligibility decision plus study-plan advice. No score, no ranking, no comparison with other candidates.

WHEN IT HAPPENS
Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "The schedule for the admission interview sessions is determined annually by the Department and is also published on the website. This schedule will include at least two sessions, corresponding to the beginning of classes and the deadline for enrollment set by the University." At least two sessions per academic year are therefore guaranteed, pegged to (i) the start of teaching (late September) and (ii) the University's enrolment cut-off (2 November 2026 for a.y. 2026/27). The concrete 2026/27 session dates were NOT found published on any unina.it page at the time of research — see uncertainty_notes.

WHO IS EXEMPT
Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "Bachelor's degree graduates who have obtained a bachelor's degree in the L34 class (Geological Sciences) or in the class 16 ex D.M. 509/1999, with a score higher than 90/110, are exempt from the verification and obtaining clearance." This exemption is defined by Italian degree-class codes and a grade on the Italian /110 scale, so in practice it applies only to Italian geology graduates. International applicants should expect to sit the interview.

HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS
The same eligibility assessment is what produces the pre-acceptance letter needed for the visa. Programme news, 6 May 2026: "all pre-enrolment applications submitted through Universitaly will be received and processed by the administrative office. The Coordinator of the programme will be provided with the applicants' curricula in order to assess their eligibility. Where the requirements are met, a pre-acceptance letter will be issued." The official 2026/2027 non-EU brochure defines the document: "A pre-acceptance letter certifies your eligibility for the selected degree programme. It is issued by the Programme Coordinator following an evaluation of the documents you have submitted." It also advises the correct order of operations: "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme before applying on Universitaly. Otherwise, if you have already submitted your pre-enrolment application on Universitaly, a dedicated team will forward your documents for evaluation. In this case, processing times may be longer."

ENGLISH PLACEMENT TEST (a separate, secondary test — only if you lack a certificate)
orientamento course sheet: "If your English language proficiency level is not officially recognized, a placement test can be provided by teachers of the course." volcanology.unina.it/about: "If the English language level is not officially recognized, a placement test can be supported by teachers of the course." This is a fallback route to prove B2, not an admission exam.

NO ITALIAN LANGUAGE TEST. Because the degree is English-taught, the Italian B2 test that international.unina.it imposes on Italian-taught degrees does not apply here.
seats_total:
NO SEAT LIMIT — the programme is open access and no maximum number of places is published on any unina.it source. This is a positive, sourced finding rather than a gap: the orientamento course sheet header states "Admission Libero", and Federico II's own definition of that status (unina.it, "Immatricolarsi alla Federico II per l'a.a. 2026/2027") is that enrolment happens directly online via Segrepass, with capped programmes handled instead through published bandi: "Questa modalità d'iscrizioni al primo anno può essere utilizzata solo per immatricolarsi ai corsi ad accesso libero; per le lauree a numero programmato la procedura si differenzia in termini di modalità e termini di scadenze a seconda dei bandi pubblicati." No such bando exists for Volcanology.

What limits intake in practice is the eligibility gate (60/24 CFU + interview + English B2), not a quota. A candidate who satisfies the requirements is not turned away because places have run out.

CONTEXT ON ACTUAL COHORT SIZE (not an official cap). The SUA-CdS repeatedly describes the programme as small and designed to be small — SUA-CdS 2026, framework B5b, justifies its tutoring model by "i numeri contenuti" (the small numbers) and notes that in-course tutoring can be delivered by the course lecturers themselves. Externally, press coverage of the programme (Nature Italy; Monocle) has described a cohort of roughly 15 mostly international students. These figures are NOT published by unina.it, are NOT a quota, and must not be presented to applicants as a competitive limit; they are included only to set realistic expectations about class size. The first graduate of the programme was Dorothea Laura Jester (Munich), who graduated with honours in July 2025 — consistent with a first intake in a.y. 2022/23 and a very small early cohort.
non_eu_reserved_seats:
[uncertain] NO reserved non-EU quota is published for this programme on any unina.it source, and structurally there is no document in which one would normally appear. Italian universities publish non-EU quotas ("contingente riservato ai cittadini non UE residenti all'estero") inside admission decrees for capped programmes; Volcanology is open access, issues no admission decree, and its orientamento sheet declares "Admission Libero". Searches of orientamento.unina.it, international.unina.it, corsi.unina.it (DH1 and P67 records and the full SUA-CdS 2026 field set), distar.unina.it and volcanology.unina.it returned no places figure of any kind, reserved or total.

The practical reading is that non-EU applicants are not competing for a fixed block of seats: they must clear the same eligibility gate as everyone else (60/24 CFU, interview, English B2), then the visa/pre-enrolment machinery. international.unina.it states the general principle for non-capped courses: candidates "have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification".

Marked uncertain because absence of a published figure is not the same as an authoritative statement that no quota exists. Universities do declare per-programme place numbers when loading courses onto the Universitaly portal, and that portal (universitaly.it, run by CINECA for the MUR) is outside the unina.it scope of this research, so a number may exist there. An applicant who needs certainty should ask master.volcanology@unina.it or pre-enrolment@unina.it directly, quoting the programme name.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH — B2 (CEFR), certified. Compulsory for applicants of every nationality, including EU and Italian applicants, and treated as an admission requirement rather than a formality. NO ITALIAN REQUIREMENT.

THE REQUIREMENT
  - Didactic Regulations, Art. 4: "Considering that the course is delivered entirely in English, proficiency in the English language equivalent to European level B2 or higher, duly certified, is required."
  - SUA-CdS 2026, REQ_ACC: "Considerato che il corso è erogato interamente in lingua inglese, è richiesta una conoscenza della lingua inglese corrispondente al livello europeo B2 o equivalente, opportunamente certificato."
  - orientamento course sheet: "English proficiency certification internationally recognized with the minimum level of language skills required in B2 (Fourth level of English within the Common Europen Framework of Reference for Languages - CEFR)."
  - volcanology.unina.it/about: "The graduate program can enroll students holding a certificate of proficiency in English internationally recognized. English level B2, i.e. the fourth level of English on the CEFR scale, is the minimum required."

ACCEPTED EVIDENCE. No single closed list of accepted certificates is published for this programme; the wording used throughout is "internationally recognized" certification at CEFR B2 or above. international.unina.it names the usual family by example — "an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.)" — and notes that such a certificate is in any case "useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation". No minimum IELTS band or TOEFL score is published anywhere on unina.it for this programme; B2 is the stated threshold and the mapping to a specific score is left to the assessing committee.

THREE EXEMPTIONS FROM PRODUCING A CERTIFICATE (identical in the Didactic Regulations, Art. 5, and SUA-CdS 2026, REQ_ACC and REQ_ACC_2). "Students will be exempt from presenting the English language certificate if they meet at least one of the following conditions:
  - Certified participation in at least one year of English language study at a secondary school;
  - Possession of a qualification obtained at English language institutes recognized as equivalent to the Italian High School Diploma;
  - Possession of a first-level degree (Bachelor equivalent) obtained from an Italian or foreign degree program delivered in English."
The third exemption is the one most international applicants will use: an English-taught bachelor's degree removes the certificate requirement outright.

FALLBACK IF YOU HAVE NEITHER A CERTIFICATE NOR AN EXEMPTION. orientamento course sheet: "If your English language proficiency level is not officially recognized, a placement test can be provided by teachers of the course." volcanology.unina.it/about repeats this. So the requirement is genuinely satisfiable in-house rather than being an absolute documentary bar.

ITALIAN — NOT REQUIRED, OFFERED AS SUPPORT. international.unina.it/admission-regulation: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." The B2 Italian rule and the Italian proficiency test described on that page apply only to Italian-taught programmes. Within the study plan, "Italian (for foreign students)/other activities" carries 6 CFU, and the orientamento sheet notes that "For students that do not need to attend Italian language courses, 6CFU of additional traineeship activities can be recognized upon request to the LM committee" — i.e. Italian is an optional support course that can be swapped for more fieldwork.

  - Opens 16 July 2026, closes 2 November 2026. unina.it news "Immatricolarsi alla Federico II per l'a.a. 2026/2027" (published 08/07/26), standfirst: "Dal 16 luglio e fino al 2 novembre, attraverso il servizio di segreteria studenti on-line 'Segrepass', è possibile iscriversi al primo anno di un corso ad accesso libero"; body: "Anche quest'anno è possibile procedere all'immatricolazione a partire dal 16 luglio e fino al 2 novembre 2026."

Didactic Regulations, Art. 5 guarantees "at least two sessions, corresponding to the beginning of classes and the deadline for enrollment set by the University" and says the calendar "is determined annually by the Department and is also published on the website". The concrete 2026/27 interview dates were NOT found published on orientamento.unina.it, volcanology.unina.it, distar.unina.it or corsi.unina.it at the time of research — this is the reason the field is marked uncertain. 1) 15 JUNE 2026 — PRE-ENROLMENT DEADLINE (ISO: 2026-06-15). The hard deadline for submitting the Universitaly pre-enrolment application naming Federico II and this programme. Brochure, Deadlines page: "JUNE 15 2026 — Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." international.unina.it repeats it identically. Because Volcanology is OPEN access, the second sentence means the door effectively closes on 15 June for this programme: after that date, pre-enrolment remains possible only for restricted-access courses. The programme's own news item of 6 May 2026 confirms: "the Universitaly platform is now open for pre-enrolment applications for our Master's Degree Programme. The platform will remain available until 15 June."

2) 30 NOVEMBER 2026 — VISA APPLICATION DEADLINE (ISO: 2026-11-30). Brochure: "NOV 30 2026 — Deadline for submitting the visa application at Italian Embassies/Consulates." Same date on international.unina.it.

3) 31 JANUARY 2027 — ENROLMENT COMPLETION DEADLINE (ISO: 2027-01-31). Brochure: "JAN 31 2027 — Deadline for completing enrolment at University of Naples Federico II. After this date students who are not officially enrolled according to ministerial regulations will have their visa revoked, and Italian police authorities will be notified."
  CAUTION — TYPO IN THE OFFICIAL BROCHURE. Its "Matriculation (final enrolment)" page says "Students who obtained visa are required to matriculate by 31 January 2026", which cannot be right for a 2026/2027 intake and contradicts the brochure's own Deadlines page. Treat 31 January 2027 as correct and verify with pre-enrolment@unina.it if it matters.

SEQUENCE AND ORDER OF OPERATIONS. Brochure, Stages: "APPLICATION: You must register on the Universitaly Portal, complete your pre-enrolment application, and submit it to the University. VALIDATION: The University will review your application, verify your admission to the selected programme, and forward your application to the Italian Embassy or Consulate in your country of residence. VISA ISSUANCE: After validation, you may schedule an appointment at the Embassy/Consulate to begin the visa application process." The University validates only once the Coordinator has issued the pre-acceptance letter: "The University will validate your application once the course coordinator has issued your pre-acceptance letter." Strong advice from the same brochure: "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme before applying on Universitaly." Practically, contact master.volcanology@unina.it with your documents WELL BEFORE 15 June.

PRE-ENROLMENT PORTAL OPENING. The portal opens in spring; the programme's earlier notice records a 2 April opening in a prior cycle ("Compulsory pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal starts on 2 April 2025") and the 2026 cycle notice is dated 6 May 2026. Expect an April-May opening, a 15 June close.

A WARNING WORTH REPEATING TO APPLICANTS. Brochure FAQ: "I have cancelled my Universitaly application to the University of Naples Federico II. Can I apply again to the same University? No, you cannot. If you cancel your application on Universitaly, you cannot reapply to the same University for the same academic year."

AFTER ARRIVAL. "Once you have travelled to Italy, you must apply for a permit of stay for study purposes within 8 days from your arrival." And: "do not withdraw (rinuncia agli studi) from your studies under any circumstances. If you withdraw, your residence permit will become invalid and you will need to apply for a new entry visa to Italy."

A CONTRADICTION ON ADMISSION LETTERS. international.unina.it/admission-regulation states: "Important! The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa." The 2026/2027 brochure and the programme's own May 2026 news item both state the opposite in substance — that a pre-acceptance letter IS issued by the Programme Coordinator and IS "a mandatory document for obtaining a study visa". The brochure and the programme news are more recent and programme-specific; the international.unina.it sentence appears to be legacy text distinguishing a formal "admission letter" from a "pre-acceptance letter". Applicants should rely on the pre-acceptance letter route.

NON-EU CITIZENS WHO DO NOT NEED A VISA (legally resident in Italy or an EU country) do NOT use this track at all. international.unina.it: they "have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification", may "present your academic documents directly to the Coordinator of the Course in which you wish to enrol", and "will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal." required_documents:
[uncertain] No single consolidated official checklist covers the whole journey. The lists below are the published official fragments, in the order a candidate needs them. Marked uncertain because the document list the programme's own admission committee expects at the ELIGIBILITY/INTERVIEW stage is nowhere published — the Regulations say only that the Committee decides "Based on the student's curriculum vitae and the outcomes of the interview".

A) ELIGIBILITY / PRE-ACCEPTANCE STAGE (all applicants)
The programme instructs candidates to send documents to the coordinator for assessment; volcanology.unina.it news: "Please also send your documents to [master.volcanology@unina.it] to speed up the pre-enrolment procedure." What the Committee assesses is the curriculum vitae plus the academic record, since the decisive checks are the degree, the 60/24 CFU profile and English B2. Expect, at minimum: degree certificate, full transcript of records with credits and disciplinary sectors, course/syllabus descriptions, CV, and the English certificate (or evidence of one of the three exemptions).
For EU / EU-equivalent candidates, international.unina.it lists what the University may require to evaluate a foreign qualification: "eventual translations; legalisations; Diploma Supplement; certificates of examinations; certificates from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA); any declarations of value issued by the competent diplomatic representations."

B) UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT — NON-EU RESIDING ABROAD (official 2026/2027 brochure, "Upload of Academic Documents (PDF format) — For Master's Programmes (Laurea Magistrale)"):
  - Transcript of Records (ToR)
  - Final degree certificate
  - Detailed course descriptions
  - Additional documents, e.g. language certificates, motivation letter, reference letters
  - Pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator
  - Declaration of Value (DoV) or CIMEA "both Statement of comparability and verification"
Plus personal data "exactly as shown on your passport", the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested, and the programme to which you have been admitted. The Italian tax code (codice fiscale) "can be left blank at this stage, but it is required for enrolment".

C) DOCUMENTS SUPPORTING THE ACADEMIC QUALIFICATION (same brochure — three alternative routes, choose the one that fits your country):
  - Declaration of Value issued by Italian Embassies/Consulates; alternatively the Statement of Comparability AND Statement of Verification issued jointly by CIMEA.
  - If the qualification was obtained in a European Higher Education Area / Bologna Process country: a Diploma Supplement accompanied by the CIMEA Statement of Verification.
  - If from a Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory country: a Statement of Correspondence via the CIMEA ARDI platform, accompanied by the CIMEA Statement of Verification.
  "At the enrolment stage, the above-mentioned documents are mandatory and must accompany the submitted/declared academic qualifications."
  Practical advice from the brochure's FAQ: "We warmly suggest that you start the process well in advance, as it may take time. Please try to avoid periods of high demand."

D) FINAL ENROLMENT (matriculation)
General University list, international.unina.it: "Copy of passport; Application form; 1 passport photo; Tax code; Residence permit (proof of having applied for it); Declaration of value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained or certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres." The page adds: "Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website."
For candidates enrolling through Segrepass, the University's open-access master's FAQ lists what must be delivered to the Student Registry desk: the printed summary of the enrolment procedure (plico), one passport-format photo (unless already uploaded), a photocopy of a valid identity document, and — if the bachelor's degree was obtained at another university — a self-certification under D.P.R. 445/2000 stating the awarding university, the exact title, the date and final grade, and the full list of examinations passed with date, grade, CFU and SSD for each.
The codice fiscale is mandatory to complete enrolment, obtainable from the Agenzia delle Entrate or an Italian embassy; the brochure notes you may start without it and that the Student Office can generate the fee payment notices in the meantime.

E) IN-COURSE, NOT FOR ADMISSION (listed only so applicants do not confuse them with entry documents). Graduation requires a Thesis Assignment Request form plus a "nulla osta" clearance form submitted at least 6 months before the graduation session with no more than 2 exams outstanding, a Graduation Application with a EUR 16 revenue stamp filed from the 1st to the 15th of the month preceding the session, and a Degree Examination Booking Form (programme Documentation page). Field and laboratory work additionally require safety training and health-surveillance clearance under D.Lgs. 81/08 (DiSTAR teaching noticeboard).

HOW THE SYSTEM WORKS. Federico II charges an ISEE/ISEEU-based contribution, not a flat programme price, so no single number applies to this degree. Key features, from the University's own summary (orientamento.unina.it, "Le tasse universitarie alla Federico II") and the open-access master's FAQ:
  - A "no tax area" up to EUR 26,000 of ISEEU — below that threshold the contribution is nil.
  - The amount is computed automatically inside Segrepass once the ISEEU is entered; ISEEU data are pulled electronically from INPS with the student's prior authorisation.
  - "Gli studenti che non inseriscono i dati ISEE pagheranno il massimo importo annualmente previsto" — students who do not submit ISEE data pay the maximum annual amount. Applicants who cannot obtain an ISEE (common for newly-arrived international students) should assume the maximum band unless the Student Office advises otherwise.
  - Merit reductions exist, including a 50% reduction for students entering a laurea magistrale having graduated from their bachelor's with 110 e lode, plus percentage reductions based on credits earned, a partial refund for graduating in the summer session of the final year, and a reduction where a household has several enrolled members.
  - Payment is split into instalments (three instalments in the cycle described on the orientamento page; the current-year schedule is published in the annual fee guide).
  - A compulsory regional tax (tassa regionale) and a EUR 16 legal stamp are added on top of the contribution.

WHY THIS FIELD IS MARKED UNCERTAIN — A FIGURE ON THE INTERNATIONAL SITE THAT DOES NOT RECONCILE. international.unina.it/admission-regulation publishes a short "Fees" block: "European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory) — Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)." Taken literally this implies non-EU students pay no tuition at all and EU students pay EUR 200. That is not consistent with the ISEE-based system described on the University's own fee pages, and no corroborating decree was found. It may describe a specific exemption category rather than the general rule. Do NOT quote these figures to applicants as the cost of this degree. The reliable procedure is: run http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ for the applicant's situation, and confirm with the Student Registry office.

SCHOLARSHIPS. Two distinct routes, neither programme-specific:
  - ADISURC / regional right-to-study grants, via https://www.unina.it/it/ateneo/concorsi-e-borse-di-studio/borse-di-studio and the "Agevolazioni e borse di studio" section of the fees hub.
  - The University's "STUDY IN NAPLES" programme (international.unina.it), funded with Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo, which awards scholarships to international students enrolling in the first year of one of Federico II's international (English-taught) courses. All students holding a degree obtained outside the Italian education system count as international regardless of citizenship, and both non-EU and EU applicants who apply for pre-admission to the international degree courses are considered. The current-year call is published under international.unina.it "Call for Applicants"; the 2026/27 call URL was not located during this research and should be checked at https://www.international.unina.it/opportunities/call-for-applicants/.

uncertainty_notes:
1) THE PAGE EXISTS AND IS REACHABLE FROM ITS SUBJECT LISTING — THE BRIEF'S FLAG IS RESOLVED AND WAS ONLY HALF-RIGHT. The brief warned the programme "may not be linked from its own subject-area listing page on orientamento.unina.it — it may only be reachable via a direct URL". Verified: the course sheet at https://www.orientamento.unina.it/corsidistudio/volcanology/ IS listed on its subject-area page, https://www.orientamento.unina.it/futuri-studenti/offerta-didattica/corsi-scienze-mmffnn/ (Scienze Matematiche Fisiche e Naturali), where it appears as "Volcanology" alongside Scienze Geologiche, Geologia e Geologia Applicata and Geoscienze. What IS true is that the top-level offerta didattica page (https://www.orientamento.unina.it/futuri-studenti/offerta-didattica/) contains no course links at all — it is a JavaScript-rendered grid of 14 subject-area tiles — so any crawler or text search that stops there will conclude the programme does not exist. The programme also has a full standalone website, volcanology.unina.it, plus records on corsi.unina.it, distar.unina.it and unina.it. Existence is not in doubt.

2) THE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: THE DEGREE CLASS AND COURSE CODE HAVE CHANGED. The brief's "LM-74" is right as a family but out of date as a code. The active course a 2026/27 applicant enters is DH1, class LM-74 R (the reformed class), "attivo": true, SUA-CdS filed for 2025 and 2026. The old course P67, class LM-74, is flagged "esaurimento": true — closed to new enrolments and running only until existing students graduate — with its last SUA in 2024 and its page headed "Regulations valid for students enrolled up to the 2024/2025 a.y.". This matters because most public pages have not caught up: the orientamento course sheet still shows "Degree class LM-74", still publishes the P67-era study plan, and search engines still surface corsi.unina.it/P67 as the canonical page. Downstream consumers of this record should present the class as "LM-74 (reformed class LM-74 R from a.y. 2025/26)" and link to https://www.corsi.unina.it/DH1, not P67.

3) THE ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS TIGHTENED BETWEEN THE TWO VERSIONS — AND THE PUBLIC PAGES SHOW THE OLD, LOOSER VERSION. The legacy Art. 4 text asked for 60 CFU spread across GEO, FIS, MAT, CHIM, ING-INF/05 and INF/01 with no minimum geoscience core. The current SUA-CdS 2026 adds a hard sub-requirement: of those 60 credits, at least 24 must sit in geoscience sectors (GEOS-01 to GEOS-04), geotechnics (CEAR-05/A) or Earth/planetary/space/climate physics (PHYS-05/B). A physics or chemistry graduate reading only the orientamento sheet ("Bachelor's (3 years minimum) in Geology, Physics or Chemistry or equivalent degree") could reasonably believe they qualify and then be refused. Note that volcanology.unina.it/about DOES state the 24-credit core, and states the entry discipline more narrowly ("A Bachelor (min 3 years) in Geology or equivalent degree"). Where the three sources disagree, the SUA-CdS 2026 and the Didactic Regulations govern.

4) "ADMISSION LIBERO" IS THE MOST MISLEADABLE FIELD IN THIS RECORD. It means no numerus clausus, no ranking and no bando — it does NOT mean automatic admission. A compulsory personal-preparation INTERVIEW before a three-professor committee, producing a written nulla-osta, stands between a candidate and enrolment, and essentially every international applicant must sit it (the exemption is defined by Italian degree-class codes and an Italian /110 grade). Any summary that renders this programme as simply "open access, no test" is materially wrong.

5) THE 2026/27 ADMISSION-INTERVIEW SESSION DATES ARE NOT PUBLISHED — THE MAIN GENUINE GAP. The Regulations promise the calendar is "determined annually by the Department and is also published on the website", with at least two sessions. No such calendar was found on orientamento.unina.it (its "Application timeline" heading is empty), volcanology.unina.it, distar.unina.it (including the teaching noticeboard) or corsi.unina.it. This is why application_deadline_eu is marked uncertain: the enrolment window (16 July - 2 November 2026) is confirmed, but the earlier interview date that actually gates enrolment is not. Applicants should email master.volcanology@unina.it well before the enrolment window opens.

6) A DATE ERROR INSIDE THE OFFICIAL NON-EU BROCHURE. Its Deadlines page gives the enrolment-completion deadline as 31 January 2027; its Matriculation page says "required to matriculate by 31 January 2026" for the same 2026/2027 intake. The Deadlines page is internally consistent with the June-2026/November-2026 sequence and should be treated as correct. Flagged because an applicant who reads only the Matriculation page could believe the deadline has already passed.

7) A CONTRADICTION ON WHETHER AN ADMISSION LETTER IS ISSUED. international.unina.it/admission-regulation says flatly "The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa", while the 2026/2027 brochure and the programme's own May 2026 news item both say a pre-acceptance letter IS issued by the Programme Coordinator and IS mandatory for the visa. The more recent, programme-specific sources should be followed; the international.unina.it sentence appears to be legacy text drawing a distinction between a formal "admission letter" and a "pre-acceptance letter". Applicants should not be discouraged by it.

8) THE FEE FIGURES ON international.unina.it DO NOT RECONCILE WITH THE UNIVERSITY'S OWN FEE SYSTEM. That page states EUR 200/year tuition for European students and no tuition line at all for non-European students, whereas unina.it describes an ISEE/ISEEU-banded contribution with a no-tax area to EUR 26,000 and a maximum band for students who file no ISEE. These cannot both be general rules. No decree reconciling them was found. tuition_or_fees_link is marked uncertain and the figures must not be presented as this programme's price; the official simulator at http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ is the only reliable instrument.

9) NO SEAT NUMBERS ARE PUBLISHED ANYWHERE ON unina.it. Neither a total cap nor a reserved non-EU quota appears in the DH1 or P67 records, the full SUA-CdS 2026 field set, the orientamento sheet, the department site or the programme site — consistent with open access. Non-official press coverage (Nature Italy, Monocle) describes a cohort of roughly 15 mostly international students, and the SUA-CdS itself refers to "numeri contenuti"; these indicate a small class, not a quota, and are recorded only as context. non_eu_reserved_seats is marked uncertain because a per-programme places figure may be declared on the Universitaly portal, which lies outside the unina.it-only scope of this research.

10) COORDINATOR OF RECORD VS DEGREE PROGRAMME DIRECTOR — NOT A CONTRADICTION, BUT WORTH KNOWING. The course register lists Daniele Morgavi (daniele.morgavi@unina.it) as coordinator for both DH1 and P67, while the orientamento sheet and the SUA-CdS both name Prof. Paola Petrosino as Degree Programme Director / "present coordinator". Both are current DiSTAR staff on this programme; the registry field and the SUA field are maintained separately and are out of step. For admission enquiries the safest address is the programme office, master.volcanology@unina.it, which is the one the programme itself publishes.

11) THE CURRENT REGULATION PDF CARRIES A STALE HEADER. The file "Regolamento LM74 R Volcanology.pdf" (filed under DH1, academic year 2025, published 24 July 2025) still shows "LM-74" in its title block and "Regulations in force since the academic year 2024-25" — carried over from the previous version. Its filename, its filing under DH1 and its 2025 academic-year record identify it as the LM-74 R regulation. The substantive articles quoted in this record (Art. 4, 5, 9, 10) are cross-checked against the independently maintained SUA-CdS 2026 fields REQ_ACC and REQ_ACC_2, which agree.
